properties.natural_language: Any SSZ-encoded data received from an untrusted peer over the Deneb light client P2P layer MUST be deserialized within a try/catch or equivalent error boundary. Malformed SSZ payloads MUST NOT cause a node crash or unbounded memory allocation.

Before processing SSZ data from a peer, the message length MUST be checked against the maximum allowed size for the specific message type. Messages exceeding the limit MUST be discarded and the peer scored negatively.
SSZ data from untrusted peers MUST be validated against the expected schema for the Deneb fork before any state mutation occurs. Fields outside the Deneb SSZ schema MUST be rejected.

The blob sidecar count sent to the execution engine via the Engine API MUST NOT exceed the maximum blob limit defined by the EIP-7928 state transition rules. The execution engine MUST reject payloads with excess blobs.
Each blob sent to the execution engine MUST have a valid KZG commitment and proof verified before crossing the consensus-execution boundary. Blobs with invalid KZG proofs MUST NOT be forwarded.

The access list RLP encoding sent to the execution engine MUST conform to the specified format with each entry being a tuple of (address, storage_keys). Malformed RLP MUST be rejected before engine processing.

A bootstrap response from a peer MUST contain a valid LightClientBootstrap object with a header whose slot is within the acceptable range. Responses with slots in the future or before the Deneb fork activation MUST be rejected.
The sync committee aggregate signature in a bootstrap response MUST be verified against the current sync committee public keys. A bootstrap with an invalid aggregate signature MUST be discarded.

A deposit submitted by a validator MUST include a valid deposit data root, the correct amount (>= MIN_DEPOSIT_AMOUNT), and a BLS signature matching the supplied public key. Invalid deposits MUST NOT be added to the deposit tree.

Before a deposit is appended to the deposit tree, the deposit contract MUST verify the deposit amount is exactly 1 Gwei granularity and the withdrawal credentials conform to the expected format (0x00 or 0x01 prefix).

A deposit snapshot received from a peer during sync MUST be verified by recomputing the Merkle root from the provided finalized deposits and comparing against a known finalized checkpoint root. Snapshots with mismatched roots MUST be rejected.

A deposit snapshot from a peer MUST include a deposit count that is less than or equal to the finalized deposit count known from the beacon chain. Snapshots claiming more deposits than finalized MUST be rejected as potentially malicious.

A withdrawal sent from the beacon chain to the execution layer MUST have a valid validator index that exists in the beacon state. The withdrawal amount MUST NOT exceed the validator's withdrawable balance.
The withdrawal address in a beacon chain withdrawal MUST be a valid 20-byte Ethereum address. Withdrawals to the zero address (0x0000...0000) MUST be rejected at the execution layer.

A block header received from the network for Cancun validation MUST contain valid parent_hash, timestamp strictly greater than parent timestamp, and base_fee_per_gas computed correctly from the parent block. Headers failing these checks MUST be rejected before full block processing.
A Cancun block header MUST set the difficulty field to 0 and the nonce field to 0x0000000000000000, as the chain is post-merge. Headers with non-zero difficulty or nonce MUST be rejected.

An attacker depositing validators to a testnet MUST still meet the minimum deposit amount and valid BLS credentials. The protocol MUST ensure that even with a large number of attacker-controlled validators, the reset mechanism can recover the network within the defined reset period.

The testnet reset mechanism MUST detect when an attacker has deposited enough validators to exceed a safety threshold (e.g., >1/3 of total stake) and MUST trigger protective measures such as rate-limiting new validator activations.

Attacker-deposited validators MUST go through the same activation queue as honest validators. The protocol MUST NOT allow bypassing the activation queue regardless of the number of deposits submitted in a single epoch.

Any input string passed to hex decoding functions MUST consist exclusively of characters in [0-9a-fA-F] optionally prefixed with '0x'. If invalid characters are present, the function MUST raise a ValueError or equivalent, never silently truncate or substitute.

The definition of 'valid hexadecimal' MUST be explicitly specified as: an even-length string of characters from [0-9a-fA-F], optionally prefixed with '0x'. Odd-length hex strings MUST be rejected or zero-padded with documented behavior.

The block access list RLP format MUST be defined as a list of (address, [storage_keys]) tuples where address is 20 bytes and each storage key is 32 bytes. Any deviation from this format MUST cause block validation to fail.

The execution engine MUST independently validate the access list entries against the transaction's actual storage accesses. The execution engine MUST NOT trust that the consensus layer has fully validated access list correctness.

All Capella light client protocol rules that are not explicitly superseded by Deneb-specific changes MUST continue to apply in the Deneb fork. The set of carried-forward rules MUST be enumerable and documented.
A peer that sends a malformed or schema-invalid light client message MUST receive a negative peer score adjustment. Repeated malformed messages from the same peer MUST result in disconnection.

The encoding of the point at infinity for BN256 (alt_bn128) curves MUST be represented as (0, 0) in the 64-byte input format. Any other encoding claiming to represent the point at infinity MUST be rejected.

When an EIP-196 precompile operation fails (invalid point, not on curve, etc.), the precompile MUST consume all provided gas and return an empty byte array. It MUST NOT return partial results or error codes in the output buffer.

If the input to an EIP-196 precompile contains surplus bytes beyond the expected input length, the surplus bytes MUST be ignored (right-truncated). The precompile MUST NOT fail due to input being longer than expected.
Precompile addresses MUST be derived from the immutable constant mapping defined in the protocol specification. No runtime mechanism may alter the address-to-precompile mapping.

The gas cost for a precompile address lookup in the dispatch mapping MUST be O(1) and MUST NOT vary based on the number of registered precompiles. The lookup itself MUST NOT consume additional gas beyond the CALL opcode overhead.

The memory expansion cost formula MUST be computed as: cost = (memory_size_word^2) / 512 + 3 * memory_size_word, where memory_size_word = ceil(size / 32). Any deviation from this quadratic formula MUST be considered a consensus bug.
When a buffer read extends beyond the current memory size, all bytes beyond the allocated region MUST be padded with zeros. The read MUST NOT return uninitialized memory content.

EVM memory MUST NOT be expanded beyond a practical maximum that would cause the quadratic gas cost to exceed the block gas limit. Any memory expansion attempt whose gas cost would exceed remaining gas MUST trigger an out-of-gas exception.

The term 'finalized' in the deposit tree context MUST consistently refer to deposits included in a finalized beacon block. The deposit tree's finalized checkpoint MUST always correspond to a beacon chain finalized checkpoint, not merely a justified one.

Pruning of deposit tree nodes MUST only remove nodes that are fully finalized and whose Merkle proof is no longer needed by any active validator. Pruning MUST NOT remove nodes that are referenced by pending deposits or non-finalized blocks.

A deposit tree snapshot taken during active deposit processing (flux) MUST either include all deposits up to a consistent cutoff point or be deferred until the current batch completes. Partial snapshots with inconsistent Merkle roots MUST be detected and rejected.

The blob_gas_used field in a Cancun block header MUST represent the total gas consumed by blob transactions in that block, while excess_blob_gas MUST be computed from the parent's excess_blob_gas and blob_gas_used. These two fields MUST NOT be conflated.

In all Cancun (post-merge) blocks, the difficulty field MUST be exactly 0 and the nonce field MUST be exactly 0x0000000000000000. Any block with non-zero values in these fields MUST be rejected as invalid.

The reset period for testnet recovery MUST have explicit upper and lower bounds defined in epochs. A reset period of zero epochs or one exceeding the weak subjectivity period MUST be considered invalid configuration.

If a client fails to download genesis state during testnet initialization, the client MUST retry with exponential backoff and MUST NOT proceed with an empty or partial genesis state. After max retries, the client MUST halt with a clear error.

The notion of a 'sufficiently large' validator set for testnet security MUST be quantified as a minimum number of validators (e.g., >= 4 * safety_decay validators). Testnet operation with fewer validators MUST trigger a warning.

MCOPY with overlapping source and destination ranges MUST behave as if the source is first copied to a temporary buffer, then written to the destination. The result MUST be equivalent to memmove semantics, not memcpy.

Memory addresses in the EVM are 256-bit values, but practical memory access MUST be bounded by gas costs. Any memory offset that, when combined with the access size, would exceed 2^32 bytes MUST be treated as an out-of-gas condition due to the quadratic memory cost.
Hex input received from external sources (RPC, config files) MUST be treated as untrusted and validated before parsing. The hex utility functions MUST NOT assume inputs are pre-sanitized.

Python's int() function used for hex parsing MUST be called with base=16 explicitly. Reliance on automatic base detection (base=0) MUST be avoided as it could accept octal or binary prefixes unexpectedly.
Type wrappers for hex-encoded values (Bytes4, Bytes32, etc.) MUST enforce length bounds at construction time. A Bytes32 wrapper receiving more or fewer than 32 bytes MUST raise an error immediately.

The consensus layer MUST trust the execution engine to correctly execute transactions, but MUST independently verify the resulting state root. If state root verification fails, the block MUST be rejected regardless of execution engine response.
Communication between the consensus layer and execution engine via the Engine API MUST use authenticated JWT tokens. Unauthenticated Engine API calls MUST be rejected.

The Deneb light client protocol MUST assume that gossip messages are eventually delivered to all honest nodes within the gossip propagation bound. Protocol correctness MUST NOT depend on instantaneous delivery.

The Deneb light client protocol MUST assume at least one honest peer in the connected peer set. If all peers are potentially dishonest, the light client MUST fall back to a trusted checkpoint sync mechanism.

The BN256 curve parameters used in EIP-196 precompiles MUST be exactly the alt_bn128 curve with the documented generator points and field prime. Any implementation MUST produce identical outputs for identical inputs across all clients.

The gas costs for EIP-196 precompiles MUST be calibrated such that the worst-case computation time at the gas limit does not exceed the block time. The gas-to-computation ratio MUST prevent denial-of-service via expensive curve operations.

The security of EIP-196 pairing checks relies on the hardness of the Discrete Logarithm Problem on the BN256 curve. The chosen curve parameters MUST provide at least 100-bit security against known attacks.

The EIP-196 precompile MUST rely on the hardness of the Discrete Logarithm Problem on the alt_bn128 curve. If DLP is broken for this curve, the pairing-based verification in the precompile is compromised.
The precompile address-to-implementation mapping MUST be immutable across the lifetime of a fork. Once deployed, a precompile address MUST always execute the same logic within that fork.
Precompile contract addresses (0x01 through 0x0a for Cancun) MUST NOT have deployable EVM bytecode. A CALL to a precompile address MUST execute the native implementation, never EVM bytecode.
The precompile dispatch mapping MUST be audited for correctness and MUST match the canonical specification. Address-to-function mapping errors can lead to wrong precompile execution.

The module path used to load precompile implementations MUST be fixed at compile time or configuration time. Dynamic module resolution for precompile implementations MUST NOT be used to prevent code injection.

Gas MUST be charged for memory expansion BEFORE the memory operation executes. If insufficient gas remains for the expansion cost, an out-of-gas exception MUST be raised without performing the memory write.
All newly allocated EVM memory MUST be initialized to zero bytes. No memory read to a previously unwritten offset may return non-zero data.
The EVM memory implementation MUST use a bytearray or equivalent safe buffer that prevents buffer overflows. Direct pointer arithmetic on the memory buffer MUST NOT be used without bounds checking.

The deposit tree protocol MUST operate under the weak subjectivity assumption: clients syncing from a recent finalized checkpoint can trust the deposit tree state at that checkpoint without replaying all deposits from genesis.

The deposit tree snapshot sync protocol assumes at least one honest peer will provide a correct snapshot. If all peers return conflicting snapshots, the client MUST fall back to full deposit log replay from a trusted execution layer endpoint.

The execution layer MUST correctly index deposit contract events by block number and log index. Missing or out-of-order deposit events MUST be detectable by comparing the deposit count in the beacon state.

The beacon chain finalization mechanism MUST eventually finalize epochs under normal network conditions. The deposit tree relies on finalization liveness to advance its finalized checkpoint and enable pruning.
The Cancun execution layer MUST trust that withdrawals provided by the beacon chain are valid and finalized. The execution layer MUST NOT independently re-validate withdrawal eligibility.

RLP encoding of Cancun blocks MUST be deterministic: the same block data MUST always produce the identical RLP byte sequence. Non-deterministic RLP encoding would cause block hash mismatches across clients.

The parent_beacon_block_root in a Cancun block header MUST correspond to an actual beacon block root. Forging this value MUST be computationally infeasible as it is verified against the beacon chain state.
Checkpoint sync for testnet recovery MUST trust the checkpoint provider to supply a valid state. The client MUST verify the checkpoint state root against a known trusted source before proceeding.

Testnet validators MUST have synchronized clocks within acceptable bounds (e.g., < 500ms drift). Clock desynchronization exceeding the slot duration MUST trigger attestation/proposal failures that are detectable.

After a testnet reset, validator clients MUST be resilient to restart: they MUST detect the new genesis and re-initialize without manual intervention. Stale state from the previous testnet instance MUST be purged.

Genesis parameters for a testnet reset (genesis time, initial validators, fork version) MUST be distributed through a trusted channel. Clients MUST NOT accept genesis parameters from untrusted P2P sources.
All newly allocated EVM memory MUST be initialized to zero. A MLOAD from a previously unwritten offset MUST return 0x00...00 (32 zero bytes).
EVM memory expansion cost MUST follow the quadratic formula: cost = 3 * words + words^2 / 512. This quadratic growth MUST prevent excessive memory allocation within the gas limit.

Each EVM execution context (call frame) MUST have its own isolated memory space. A CALL to another contract MUST NOT allow the callee to read or write the caller's memory, except through explicit CALLDATA/RETURNDATA mechanisms.
MSTORE8 MUST write only the least significant byte of the provided value to the target memory offset. The upper 31 bytes of the 256-bit value MUST be masked off and discarded.
After a successful ECADD operation, the output point MUST lie on the alt_bn128 curve. If the output does not satisfy the curve equation y^2 = x^3 + 3, the implementation has a bug.
After a successful ECMUL operation with scalar k and point P, the output MUST equal k*P computed over the alt_bn128 curve group. Multiplying by 0 MUST yield the point at infinity.
After a successful pairing check, the precompile MUST return exactly 32 bytes: 0x...01 if the pairing equation holds, or 0x...00 if it does not. No other return values are permitted.
After dispatching to a precompile, if the precompile returns success, the return data MUST be placed in the caller's return buffer. The gas remaining MUST reflect the precompile's gas consumption.

After dispatching to a non-existent precompile address (address > highest defined precompile), the CALL MUST behave as a call to an empty account: succeed with no return data and consume only the base call gas.
After a deposit is successfully appended to the deposit tree, the tree's deposit count MUST increment by exactly 1, and the new Merkle root MUST be recomputable from the updated leaf set.

After deposit tree finalization advances, all deposits up to the new finalized index MUST have their Merkle proofs verifiable against the finalized root. The finalized deposit count MUST be monotonically non-decreasing.

After successfully loading a deposit snapshot from a peer, the local deposit tree state MUST match the snapshot's Merkle root, deposit count, and finalized epoch. The client MUST be able to continue appending new deposits on top of the snapshot.

After processing all withdrawals in a Cancun block, the sum of withdrawal amounts MUST equal the total balance change across all withdrawal recipient addresses. No ETH may be created or destroyed during withdrawal processing.

After successful Cancun block validation, the excess_blob_gas for the next block MUST be computed as: max(0, parent.excess_blob_gas + parent.blob_gas_used - TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK). This value MUST be stored for the next block's base blob fee calculation.

After a Cancun block is fully validated, the parent_beacon_block_root MUST be stored in the beacon roots contract at address 0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02 indexed by timestamp. This storage MUST be verifiable by subsequent blocks.
After block header validation completes for a Cancun block, the block MUST have a valid blob_gas_used value that is a multiple of GAS_PER_BLOB (2^17) and does not exceed MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK.
After a testnet reset is triggered, a new genesis state MUST be created with the specified initial validator set. The old chain state MUST be fully discarded and unreachable from the new chain.

After a testnet reset, all previously active validators (including attacker-controlled ones) MUST be removed from the active validator set. Only validators in the new genesis deposit list MUST be active.

After the execution engine processes a block with an access list, the gas charged for storage accesses in the access list MUST use the warm storage cost (100 gas) rather than the cold cost (2600 gas) for all listed slots.

After blob validation in the EIP-7928 state transition, the number of blobs included in the block MUST match the number of blob commitments in the block header. Any mismatch MUST cause block rejection.

After hex encoding a byte sequence, the output string MUST have exactly twice the length of the input bytes (excluding any '0x' prefix). The round-trip encode(decode(x)) MUST equal x for all valid hex strings.
After hex decoding a valid hex string, the output byte length MUST equal len(input) / 2 (excluding '0x' prefix). Each pair of hex characters MUST map to exactly one byte.

After MSTORE executes, the 32 bytes starting at the target offset MUST contain the big-endian representation of the stored value. The memory size MUST be updated to at least offset + 32 if it was previously smaller.

After MCOPY executes with length L from source S to destination D, the bytes at [D, D+L) MUST be identical to the bytes that were at [S, S+L) before the operation. Memory size MUST be updated to cover both source and destination ranges.

After MLOAD executes at offset O, the returned 256-bit value MUST equal the big-endian interpretation of the 32 bytes at memory positions [O, O+32). Memory MUST be expanded to at least O+32 if needed.
After a Cancun memory operation that triggers expansion, the memory size reported by MSIZE MUST be a multiple of 32 bytes (word-aligned) and MUST be >= the highest accessed offset + access size.

After a LightClientUpdate is successfully validated and applied, the light client's stored finalized header MUST advance to a slot >= the previous finalized slot. The finalized header MUST NOT regress.

After processing a LightClientOptimisticUpdate, the optimistic header slot MUST be >= the previously stored optimistic header slot. The sync committee signature MUST have been verified before acceptance.

The ECADD precompile at address 0x06 MUST charge exactly 150 gas. The ECMUL precompile at address 0x07 MUST charge exactly 6000 gas. The pairing precompile at address 0x08 MUST charge 45000 + 34000 * k gas where k is the number of point pairs.
Input points to the ECADD precompile MUST be validated to lie on the alt_bn128 curve before addition is performed. Points not satisfying y^2 = x^3 + 3 (mod p) MUST cause the precompile to fail.
The scalar input to ECMUL MUST be interpreted as a 256-bit unsigned integer in big-endian format. Scalars larger than the curve order MUST be reduced modulo the curve order before multiplication.

Before dispatching a CALL to a precompile, the EVM MUST verify that sufficient gas is available for the precompile's base cost. If insufficient gas, the call MUST fail without executing the precompile.
After the SHA256 precompile (address 0x02) executes, the output MUST be exactly 32 bytes containing the SHA-256 hash of the input. The output length MUST always be 32 regardless of input length.

After the ECRECOVER precompile (address 0x01) executes with a valid signature, the output MUST be the 32-byte zero-padded address of the signer. Invalid signatures MUST return empty output (not an error).

Before processing a Cancun block, the parent block hash referenced in the header MUST exist in the node's block database. Processing a block with an unknown parent MUST be deferred until the parent is received.

After applying all transactions in a Cancun block, the transaction trie root computed from the executed transactions MUST match the transactions_root in the block header. A mismatch MUST cause block rejection.

Before processing a deposit from the deposit contract, the beacon node MUST verify the deposit's Merkle proof against the deposit root in the beacon block body. Deposits with invalid proofs MUST be skipped.
Hex encoding and decoding functions MUST be pure functions: given the same input, they MUST always produce the same output. No internal state may affect the encoding or decoding result.
The total blob gas in a block MUST NOT exceed the dynamically adjusted maximum defined by EIP-7928. The maximum MUST be computed from the target and actual blob usage of recent blocks.

All precompile implementations MUST be deterministic: given the same input bytes and gas, every client implementation MUST produce byte-identical output. Non-determinism in precompile output is a consensus-critical bug.

After CALLDATACOPY copies calldata into memory, bytes beyond the calldata length MUST be zero-padded. The memory region [destOffset, destOffset+length) MUST contain calldata[offset:offset+length] with zero-padding for out-of-bounds bytes.

After a successful checkpoint sync following testnet reset, the client's head MUST be at or after the provided checkpoint slot. The client MUST be able to validate and append new blocks from that point forward.
After MSTORE8 writes a single byte at offset O, only the byte at position O MUST be modified. All other memory bytes MUST remain unchanged.

The Deneb light client MUST only accept LightClientUpdate messages where the sync committee signature includes participation from more than 2/3 of the committee members. Updates with insufficient participation MUST be rejected.
The maximum number of withdrawals per Cancun block MUST be exactly MAX_WITHDRAWALS_PER_PAYLOAD (16). Blocks containing more than 16 withdrawals MUST be rejected.
The deposit tree MUST maintain the Merkle tree invariant at all times: every internal node MUST equal the hash of its two children. Any violation of this invariant indicates tree corruption.

Input coordinates to EIP-196 precompiles MUST be less than the field prime p = 21888242871839275222246405745257275088696311157297823662689037894645226208583. Coordinates >= p MUST cause the precompile to fail.

The MSIZE opcode MUST return the highest multiple-of-32 memory offset that has been accessed (read or written) during the current execution context. MSIZE MUST be monotonically non-decreasing within a single context.

After EIP-7928 state transition completes for a block, the blob base fee for the next block MUST be updated according to the exponential pricing formula. The fee MUST increase if blob usage exceeded the target and decrease otherwise.

Before executing the MODEXP precompile (address 0x05), the base length, exponent length, and modulus length MUST be read from the first 96 bytes of input. If the modulus is zero, the precompile MUST return zero.
